pk.context: 5 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: pale yellow, film-coated, round and curved tablet

clues.kinetics: Food has no relevant effect on exposure. It is predominantly bound to serum albumin, with an 11% free fraction, and is metabolized mainly by flavin monooxygenases 1 and 3.
clues.substance: A small molecule with a molecular weight of 401.46, supplied as a powder in an amber glass bottle to be constituted with purified water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as a 60 mg powder that makes a 0.75 mg/mL oral solution, and as 5 mg tablets, taken once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning and no contraindications. Fever, diarrhea and rash are the most common adverse reactions.
clues.indication: Spinal muscular atrophy in pediatric and adult patients.
clues.mechanism: A splicing modifier of SMN2 that increases exon 7 inclusion in its mRNA and production of full-length SMN protein in the brain.

tell: A small-molecule SMN2 splicing modifier taken orally once daily, with a terminal half-life of about 50 hours.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: the median time to reach maximum plasma concentration (T max ) was 3.26 to 4 hours
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The terminal elimination half-life of risdiplam was approximately 50 hours
